subject: BAR
title: Marchetti Industrial Products: Cost of Capital and Project Selection
scenario:
Marchetti Industrial Products, Inc. (Marchetti) manufactures precision metal components. At its December 2026 meeting, the board of directors asked the controller to evaluate a proposal to install an automated finishing line and to review the company's financing mix. Marchetti's marginal income tax rate is 25%.

The capital committee has narrowed the expansion to two mutually exclusive proposals and will fund only one of them. Separately, the chief financial officer has proposed a recapitalization in which Marchetti would issue $15,000,000 of additional long-term debt and use the entire proceeds to repurchase common shares having an equal market value. Total capital measured at market value would be unchanged.

Use **Exhibit 1** through **Exhibit 4** to complete the tasks. All amounts are in U.S. dollars.

exhibits.title: Exhibit 1: Capital Structure, Market Data, and Loan Covenants at December 31, 2026
exhibits.content:
| Item | Amount or rate |
| --- | --- |
| Long-term debt — market value | $40,000,000 |
| Common equity — market value | $60,000,000 |
| Pretax yield on outstanding long-term debt | 8.0% |
| Risk-free rate | 4.5% |
| Market risk premium | 5.5% |
| Beta of Marchetti common shares | 1.30 |
| Marginal income tax rate | 25% |

The master loan agreement with Marchetti's lending group contains the following covenants:

- Total debt may not exceed 50% of total capital, with debt and equity measured at market value.
- Interest coverage, defined as earnings before interest and taxes divided by interest expense, must be at least 4.0 times. Coverage for 2026 was 5.1 times.

exhibits.title: Exhibit 2: Project Alpha — Automated Finishing Line
exhibits.content:
| Item | Amount |
| --- | --- |
| Equipment cost, payable at inception | $6,000,000 |
| Increase in net working capital at inception | $500,000 |
| Economic life and tax recovery period | 4 years |
| Tax depreciation method | Straight-line to a zero tax basis |
| Annual incremental revenue less incremental cash operating expenses | $2,600,000 |
| Estimated cash proceeds on disposal at the end of Year 4 | $800,000 |
| Engineering feasibility study completed and paid in September 2026 | $180,000 |

Additional information:

- The increase in net working capital is recovered in full at the end of Year 4.
- Incremental operating amounts are level in each of Years 1 through 4 and are assumed to occur at each year-end.
- Any gain on disposal is taxed at the marginal income tax rate.
- Marchetti evaluates expansion proposals at a risk-adjusted discount rate of 10%, which exceeds its weighted average cost of capital because of the process technology risk of the finishing line.

exhibits.title: Exhibit 3: Alternative Proposals Reviewed by the Capital Committee
exhibits.content:
**Project Beta — Rebuild of the existing finishing cells.** Project Beta is mutually exclusive with Project Alpha. Its net incremental after-tax cash flows are:

| Year | Net incremental after-tax cash flow |
| --- | --- |
| 0 | $(6,500,000) |
| 1 | $3,200,000 |
| 2 | $2,600,000 |
| 3 | $1,300,000 |
| 4 | $900,000 |

Using the same 10% risk-adjusted discount rate, the controller's staff computed the following for Project Beta:

| Measure | Result |
| --- | --- |
| Net present value | $149,273 |
| Payback period | 2.5 years |

**Project Gamma — Second distribution warehouse.** The sponsoring division withdrew Project Gamma in March 2026 and the capital committee removed it from the 2027 capital plan. No further analysis of Project Gamma was performed.

tasks.title: Weighted average cost of capital
tasks.instruction: Using the market values in Exhibit 1, calculate Marchetti's weighted average cost of capital. Determine the cost of equity under the capital asset pricing model and the cost of debt on an after-tax basis. Enter the answer as a percentage rounded to one decimal place (for example, enter 8.75% as 8.8). Do not enter a percent sign.
tasks.explanation: Cost of equity under the capital asset pricing model = risk-free rate + (beta x market risk premium) = 4.5% + (1.30 x 5.5%) = 4.5% + 7.15% = 11.65%. After-tax cost of debt = 8.0% x (1 - 0.25) = 6.0%. Market-value weights: debt = $40,000,000 / $100,000,000 = 40%; equity = $60,000,000 / $100,000,000 = 60%. Weighted average cost of capital = (0.40 x 6.0%) + (0.60 x 11.65%) = 2.40% + 6.99% = 9.39%, which is 9.4% rounded to one decimal place.
references: Corporate finance — weighted average cost of capital
Corporate finance — capital asset pricing model

tasks.title: Incremental cash flow schedule for Project Alpha
tasks.instruction: Complete the incremental cash flow schedule for Project Alpha using Exhibit 2. Years 2 and 3 are identical to Year 1 and are therefore not shown. Enter cash outflows as negative amounts, enter 0 in any cell in which no amount belongs, and enter whole dollars without commas.
tasks.explanation: Annual tax depreciation = $6,000,000 / 4 = $1,500,000. Annual after-tax operating cash flow = ($2,600,000 x 0.75) + ($1,500,000 x 0.25) = $1,950,000 + $375,000 = $2,325,000; the second term is the depreciation tax shield. Year 0 consists of the $6,000,000 equipment outlay and the $500,000 increase in net working capital, for a net outflow of $6,500,000. The engineering feasibility study was paid before the decision date and is not an incremental cash flow of the proposal. Year 4 adds the recovery of the $500,000 of net working capital and the after-tax disposal proceeds. The tax basis of the equipment at the end of Year 4 is zero, so the entire $800,000 of proceeds is a taxable gain and the after-tax amount is $800,000 - ($800,000 x 0.25) = $600,000. Net Year 4 cash flow = $2,325,000 + $500,000 + $600,000 = $3,425,000.
references: Capital budgeting — incremental after-tax cash flows
Capital budgeting — depreciation tax shield and working capital recovery

tasks.title: Net present value of Project Alpha
tasks.instruction: Using the net incremental cash flows of Project Alpha and the 10% present value factors in Exhibit 4, calculate the net present value of Project Alpha. Enter the answer in whole dollars, no commas. Enter a negative amount with a leading minus sign.
tasks.explanation: Discount each net incremental cash flow at 10%: Year 1 through Year 3 = $2,325,000 each and Year 4 = $3,425,000. Years 1 through 3 = $2,325,000 x 2.4869 = $5,782,043. Year 4 = $3,425,000 x 0.6830 = $2,339,275. Total present value of the inflows = $8,121,318. Net present value = $8,121,318 - $6,500,000 initial investment = $1,621,318, which is approximately $1,621,252 when unrounded present value factors are used. The net present value is positive, so Project Alpha increases shareholder value at the 10% risk-adjusted rate.
tasks.explanationJa:
1. Year 1〜3 は毎年 $2,325,000、Year 4 は $3,425,000（Work Tab 2 のスケジュール）
2. **Year 1〜3**: $2,325,000 × 2.4869（3年の年金現価係数）= $5,782,043
3. **Year 4**: $3,425,000 × 0.6830 = $2,339,275
4. キャッシュインフローの現在価値合計 = $5,782,043 + $2,339,275 = $8,121,318
5. **NPV** = $8,121,318 − $6,500,000（Year 0 の正味投資額）= 約 **$1,621,300**
   - 係数を丸めずに計算すると $1,621,252。丸め幅の違いは許容範囲に収まる
6. NPV がプラスなので、割引率10%のもとで Project Alpha は企業価値を増加させる
references: Corporate finance — present value of future cash flows

tasks.title: Payback period of Project Alpha
tasks.instruction: Calculate the payback period of Project Alpha, measured against the total initial investment including the increase in net working capital and assuming that cash flows accrue evenly within each year. Enter the number of years rounded to one decimal place (for example, enter three and one quarter years as 3.3).
tasks.explanation: The initial investment is $6,500,000, made up of the $6,000,000 equipment cost and the $500,000 increase in net working capital. Cumulative cash inflows are $2,325,000 after Year 1 and $4,650,000 after Year 2, leaving $6,500,000 - $4,650,000 = $1,850,000 to be recovered during Year 3. Year 3 provides $2,325,000, so the fraction of Year 3 required is $1,850,000 / $2,325,000 = 0.80 of a year. Payback period = 2 + 0.80 = 2.8 years.
references: Capital budgeting — limitations of non-discounted measures

tasks.title: Recommendation to the capital committee
tasks.instruction: The capital committee will fund only one of the two mutually exclusive proposals. Select the recommendation that is supported by the analysis.
options: Project Alpha, because it has the higher net present value
Project Beta, because it has the shorter payback period
Project Beta, because it recovers the initial investment before the equipment is fully depreciated
Neither proposal, because the payback period of each exceeds two years
tasks.correctAnswer: Project Alpha, because it has the higher net present value
tasks.explanation: For mutually exclusive proposals, the measure that ranks alternatives correctly is net present value, because it measures the dollar amount of value added at the required rate of return. Project Alpha's net present value of approximately $1,621,252 far exceeds Project Beta's net present value of $149,273. Project Beta recovers its initial investment sooner, 2.5 years against 2.8 years, but the payback period ignores the time value of money and ignores every cash flow arising after the investment is recovered, so it is not a valid basis for ranking. Both proposals have a positive net present value, so rejecting both would forgo value. Project Alpha should be recommended.
tasks.explanationJa:
相互排他的な案の順位づけには **NPV** を使う。NPV は要求収益率を満たしたうえで企業価値がいくら増えるかを金額で示すためである。

| | Project Alpha | Project Beta |
| --- | --- | --- |
| NPV | 約 $1,621,252 | $149,273 |
| 回収期間 | 2.8年 | 2.5年 |

- 回収期間は Beta の方が短いが、回収期間法は**貨幣の時間価値**と**回収後のキャッシュフロー**を無視する。Alpha は Year 4 に運転資本の回収と処分収入が入るが、回収期間法ではこれが評価に反映されない
- 両案とも NPV はプラスなので「どちらも却下」は価値を捨てることになる
- したがって **NPV の大きい Project Alpha** を推奨する
references: Capital budgeting — ranking mutually exclusive projects
Capital budgeting — net present value versus payback period

tasks.title: Effects of the proposed recapitalization
tasks.instruction: The chief financial officer proposes to issue $15,000,000 of additional long-term debt and to repurchase common shares of an equal market value. Select every statement that correctly describes an effect of the proposed recapitalization.
options: The covenant limiting total debt to 50% of total capital would be violated.
The cost of equity would rise because financial leverage increases the risk borne by common shareholders.
Interest expense would increase, which lowers the interest coverage ratio.
The after-tax cost of debt would stay at 6.0% no matter how much leverage is added.
The weighted average cost of capital must decline because debt is a cheaper source of funds than equity.
Substituting debt for equity reduces the amount of financing cost that is deductible for income tax purposes.
correctAnswer: The covenant limiting total debt to 50% of total capital would be violated.
The cost of equity would rise because financial leverage increases the risk borne by common shareholders.
Interest expense would increase, which lowers the interest coverage ratio.
tasks.explanation: After the recapitalization, debt is $40,000,000 + $15,000,000 = $55,000,000 and equity is $60,000,000 - $15,000,000 = $45,000,000, so total capital remains $100,000,000 and the debt ratio becomes 55%. That exceeds the 50% ceiling in the master loan agreement, so the leverage covenant would be violated. Additional borrowing raises interest expense, and because earnings before interest and taxes are unaffected by how the company is financed, interest coverage falls from the 5.1 times reported for 2026 and moves toward the 4.0 times floor. Higher leverage also makes the residual claim of the common shareholders more variable, so the cost of equity rises. The after-tax cost of debt does not stay fixed at 6.0%: as leverage rises, lenders price additional default risk into the yield they require. The weighted average cost of capital does not necessarily decline, because the lower weight on the more expensive equity is offset by the higher cost of equity and, beyond some level of leverage, by a higher cost of debt as well. Substituting debt for equity increases deductible financing cost rather than reducing it, because interest is deductible while dividends paid on common shares are not.
tasks.explanationJa:
**組替後の資本構成**: 負債 $40,000,000 + $15,000,000 = $55,000,000、自己資本 $60,000,000 − $15,000,000 = $45,000,000、総資本は $100,000,000 のまま → 負債比率 **55%**

正しい記述:

1. **財務制限条項の抵触** — 負債比率 55% は融資契約の上限 50% を超えるため、レバレッジ条項に抵触する
2. **自己資本コストの上昇** — レバレッジが上がると残余請求権である株主のリターンの振れ幅が大きくなるため、株主が要求する収益率は上昇する
3. **インタレスト・カバレッジの低下** — 借入残高が増えれば支払利息が増える。EBIT は資金調達方法に左右されないため、2026年の5.1倍から下限の4.0倍に近づく

誤りの記述:

- **税引後の負債コストが6.0%のまま** — レバレッジが上がれば貸手はデフォルト・リスクの増大を利回りに織り込むため、税引前利回り自体が上昇する
- **WACCは必ず下がる** — 割安な負債のウェイトが増える効果は、自己資本コストの上昇（および一定水準を超えた後の負債コストの上昇）で相殺される。必ず下がるとは言えない
- **損金算入できる資金調達コストが減る** — 逆である。支払利息は損金算入できるが普通株式の配当はできないため、負債への置換は損金算入額を**増やす**
references: Corporate finance — capital structure and financial leverage
Debt covenants — leverage and interest coverage ratios

subject: BAR
title: Mutually Exclusive Equipment Projects — Brightwater Packaging
scenario:
Brightwater Packaging Co. is evaluating two mutually exclusive projects to expand capacity at its bottling plant: Project A, a new automated filling line, and Project B, an upgrade of the existing line. Both projects have 4-year lives, and the company is not subject to capital rationing.

Assumptions:
- The income tax rate is 25%, and taxes are paid in the year the related income arises.
- For tax purposes, equipment is depreciated straight-line over 4 years to a zero salvage value (no half-year convention).
- Operating cash flows occur at the end of each year. For payback calculations only, assume cash flows occur evenly throughout each year.
- The hurdle rate is the company's weighted average cost of capital (WACC), computed with market-value weights and rounded to the nearest whole percent.
- Use the present value factors in **Exhibit 3** (do not compute your own factors).

Use **Exhibit 1** (project data), **Exhibit 2** (capital structure data), and **Exhibit 3** (present value factors and treasury summary) to complete the tasks.

exhibits.title: Exhibit 1: Project Data
exhibits.content:
| Item | Project A: Automated line | Project B: Line upgrade |
|---|---|---|
| Equipment cost (Year 0) | $400,000 | $150,000 |
| Useful life | 4 years | 4 years |
| Annual pre-tax cash operating savings (Years 1-4) | $150,000 | $65,000 |
| Working capital required at Year 0 (fully recovered at end of Year 4) | $40,000 | $0 |
| Expected selling price of equipment at end of Year 4 | $30,000 | $0 |
| Feasibility study paid last year | $12,000 | $5,000 |

Project A would be installed in floor space that is currently unused and has no alternative use.

exhibits.title: Exhibit 2: Capital Structure and Cost of Capital Data
exhibits.content:
| Source | Book value | Market value |
|---|---|---|
| Long-term debt | $3,200,000 | $3,000,000 |
| Common equity | $4,500,000 | $7,000,000 |

| Item | Rate |
|---|---|
| Coupon rate on outstanding bonds | 6.5% |
| Yield to maturity on outstanding bonds (pre-tax cost of debt) | 8.0% |
| Risk-free rate | 4.0% |
| Expected return on the market portfolio | 10.0% |
| Brightwater's equity beta | 1.3 |
| Income tax rate | 25% |

The cost of equity is estimated using the capital asset pricing model.

exhibits.title: Exhibit 3: Present Value Factors and Treasury Summary
exhibits.content:
**Present value of $1 (rounded to three decimals)**

| Year | 10% | 12% |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | 0.909 | 0.893 |
| 2 | 0.826 | 0.797 |
| 3 | 0.751 | 0.712 |
| 4 | 0.683 | 0.636 |

**Preliminary results prepared by the treasury staff**

| Measure | Project A | Project B |
|---|---|---|
| Internal rate of return | 13.8% | 20.2% |

tasks.title: Weighted average cost of capital
tasks.instruction: Using Exhibit 2, calculate Brightwater's after-tax WACC using market-value weights and the CAPM cost of equity. Enter the WACC as a percentage rounded to two decimal places (for example, enter 9.25 for 9.25%).
tasks.explanation: Cost of equity (CAPM) = 4.0% + 1.3 x (10.0% - 4.0%) = 11.8%. After-tax cost of debt = 8.0% x (1 - 0.25) = 6.0% (the yield to maturity, not the coupon rate, is the current cost of debt). Market-value weights: debt $3,000,000 / $10,000,000 = 30%; equity $7,000,000 / $10,000,000 = 70%. WACC = 0.30 x 6.0% + 0.70 x 11.8% = 1.80% + 8.26% = 10.06%. Rounded to the nearest whole percent, the hurdle rate is 10%.
references: AICPA BAR Blueprint Area I — Cost of capital (WACC, CAPM)

tasks.title: Project A cash flows
tasks.instruction: Using Exhibit 1 and the scenario assumptions, determine the following after-tax cash flows for Project A. Enter amounts in whole dollars (no commas). Enter net cash outflows as negative numbers.

rows: After-tax cash operating savings (each year, Years 1-4)
After-tax proceeds from sale of equipment (Year 4)

cells.rowLabel: After-tax cash operating savings (each year, Years 1-4)
After-tax proceeds from sale of equipment (Year 4)

tasks.explanation: After-tax savings = $150,000 x (1 - 0.25) = $112,500. Annual tax depreciation = $400,000 / 4 = $100,000; tax shield = $100,000 x 25% = $25,000. At the end of Year 4 the tax basis is zero, so the entire $30,000 sale price is a taxable gain: after-tax proceeds = $30,000 - ($30,000 x 25%) = $22,500. Year 0 = -($400,000 equipment + $40,000 working capital) = -$440,000. Year 4 = $112,500 + $25,000 + $22,500 salvage + $40,000 working capital recovery = $200,000 (Years 1-3 are $137,500 each). The $12,000 feasibility study is a sunk cost and the unused floor space has no opportunity cost, so neither is included.
references: AICPA BAR Blueprint Area I — Capital budgeting (after-tax cash flows)

tasks.title: NPV and profitability index
tasks.instruction: Using the hurdle rate and the present value factors in Exhibit 3, calculate the net present value and the profitability index for each project. Define the profitability index as the present value of Years 1-4 cash flows divided by the Year 0 net investment. Enter NPV in whole dollars (no commas) and the profitability index rounded to two decimal places.
references: AICPA BAR Blueprint Area I — Capital budgeting (NPV, profitability index)

tasks.title: Project B payback periods
tasks.instruction: Calculate the payback period and the discounted payback period for Project B, assuming cash flows occur evenly throughout each year. For the discounted payback period, use the hurdle rate and the factors in Exhibit 3. Enter each answer in years rounded to two decimal places.
tasks.explanation: Payback = $150,000 / $58,125 = 2.58 years. Discounted cash flows at 10%: Year 1 $58,125 x 0.909 = $52,836; Year 2 x 0.826 = $48,011; Year 3 x 0.751 = $43,652; Year 4 x 0.683 = $39,699. Cumulative after Year 3 = $144,499, leaving $150,000 - $144,499 = $5,501 to recover. Discounted payback = 3 + $5,501 / $39,699 = 3.14 years.
references: AICPA BAR Blueprint Area I — Capital budgeting (payback and discounted payback)

tasks.title: Investment decision
tasks.instruction: Considering your results and the IRRs in Exhibit 3, which recommendation is most appropriate?
options: Accept Project A, because it has the higher NPV and the projects are mutually exclusive with no capital rationing
Accept Project B, because it has the higher IRR
Accept Project B, because it has the higher profitability index
Accept both projects, because each has a positive NPV
tasks.correctAnswer: Accept Project A, because it has the higher NPV and the projects are mutually exclusive with no capital rationing
tasks.explanation: Both projects have IRRs above the 10% hurdle rate and positive NPVs, but only one can be chosen. When mutually exclusive projects are ranked differently by NPV and IRR (or the profitability index) and capital is not rationed, NPV governs because it measures the absolute increase in shareholder wealth: Project A adds $38,425 versus $34,198 for Project B. The profitability index is useful for ranking under capital rationing, which does not apply here.
tasks.explanationJa: 両案ともIRRがハードルレート10%を上回りNPVも正だが、相互排他なので1案しか選べない。NPVとIRR（または収益性指数）で順位が食い違い、資本制約がない場合は、株主価値の増加額を直接示す**NPVを優先**する。案AのNPV $38,425 は案Bの $34,198 を上回るため、**案Aを採用**する。収益性指数は資本制約下での順位付けに有用だが、本問には当てはまらない。
references: AICPA BAR Blueprint Area I — Capital budgeting (mutually exclusive projects)

tasks.title: Why NPV and IRR rankings conflict
tasks.instruction: Select each statement that helps explain why NPV and IRR rank Projects A and B differently. Select all that apply.
options: The projects differ significantly in the scale of the initial investment.
The IRR method implicitly assumes interim cash flows are reinvested at each project's IRR, while NPV assumes reinvestment at the cost of capital.
Project A receives a larger share of its total cash inflows at the end of its life than Project B does.
NPV ignores cash flows that occur after the payback period.
The feasibility study costs were included in the IRR calculation but not in the NPV calculation.
correctAnswer: The projects differ significantly in the scale of the initial investment.
The IRR method implicitly assumes interim cash flows are reinvested at each project's IRR, while NPV assumes reinvestment at the cost of capital.
Project A receives a larger share of its total cash inflows at the end of its life than Project B does.
tasks.explanation: Ranking conflicts arise from differences in scale ($440,000 versus $150,000 invested) and in the timing of cash flows, combined with the different reinvestment rate assumptions of the two methods. Project A's Year 4 inflow of $200,000 is about 33% of its total inflows of $612,500, compared with 25% for Project B, so Project A is relatively more back-loaded and is penalized more heavily at higher discount rates. NPV includes all cash flows over the project life (it is payback that ignores later cash flows), and the feasibility costs are sunk and excluded from both measures.
tasks.explanationJa:
NPVとIRRの順位が食い違う主な原因は次のとおり。
- **投資規模の差**：案A $440,000 に対し案B $150,000
- **再投資率の仮定の違い**：IRRは中間CFを各案のIRRで、NPVは資本コストで再投資すると暗黙に仮定する
- **CFのタイミングの差**：案Aは4年目の流入 $200,000 が総流入 $612,500 の約33%（案Bは25%）と後半に偏るため、高い割引率で不利になる

誤り：NPVは全期間のCFを含む（後半のCFを無視するのは回収期間法）。フィージビリティ調査費は埋没原価でどちらの指標にも含めない。
references: AICPA BAR Blueprint Area I — Capital budgeting (NPV versus IRR)
